title: Streaming LLM Responses
summary: Deliver incremental model output with explicit completion, cancellation, validation, and reconnect semantics rather than treating chunks as a finished answer.
overview: Streaming sends generated output incrementally, often through server-sent events or a similar transport. It improves perceived responsiveness by exposing useful progress before generation completes, but it does not necessarily reduce total generation time. Time to first token, inter-token delay, and time to a complete usable answer are separate measurements.

A stream is a protocol with intermediate and terminal states. Text fragments, tool-call arguments, usage information, errors, and completion events may arrive differently across providers. The application must buffer incomplete structured data, propagate cancellation, and decide which content is safe to display before full validation. Once text is shown, later validation cannot make the earlier disclosure disappear.

production.poc: A prototype renders chunks while distinguishing an in-progress answer from a completed one.
production.production: Production defines event schemas, terminal states, proxy buffering behavior, cancellation, and safe handling of partial tool calls.
production.scale: Enterprise scale measures active connections, slow consumers, reconnect behavior, and moderation or validation policies for incremental content.

components.name: Provider stream adapter
components.role: Normalizes provider-specific events into a stable application protocol.

components.name: Validation buffer
components.role: Holds incomplete structured or policy-sensitive content until release conditions pass.

components.name: Streaming gateway
components.role: Forwards events with bounded buffering and backpressure.

components.name: Client state machine
components.role: Tracks connecting, generating, completed, interrupted, and cancelled states.

components.name: Cancellation controller
components.role: Stops downstream generation and releases resources when work is abandoned.

flow.title: Open the response channel
flow.description: Authenticate and send an explicit start event with request identity.

flow.title: Normalize incoming events
flow.description: Separate text, tool-call fragments, status, usage, and terminal events.

flow.title: Apply release policy
flow.description: Buffer content that requires complete validation and emit only eligible fragments.

flow.title: Handle backpressure
flow.description: Bound queued bytes and disconnect or slow production when the consumer cannot keep up.

flow.title: Commit completion
flow.description: Mark the answer complete only after the terminal event and required validation pass.

flow.title: Cancel or recover
flow.description: Propagate disconnects and present interrupted output honestly; restart only under a defined replay policy.

diagrams.title: Streaming with an explicit terminal state
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
 participant P as Model provider
 participant G as Stream gateway
 participant V as Validation buffer
 participant C as Client
 P-->>G: Output event
 G->>V: Normalize and validate fragment
 V-->>C: Eligible partial content
 P-->>G: Terminal completion event
 G-->>C: Complete answer state
 C->>G: Cancel if abandoned
 G->>P: Cancel generation
diagrams.caption: Partial content remains provisional until completion and any required validation have succeeded.

diagrams.title: Client-visible stream states
diagrams.code:
stateDiagram-v2
 [*] --> Connecting
 Connecting --> Generating: Start event
 Generating --> Complete: Validated terminal event
 Generating --> Interrupted: Transport loss or provider error
 Generating --> Cancelled: User stops request
 Interrupted --> Connecting: Explicit restart permitted
 Complete --> [*]
 Cancelled --> [*]
diagrams.caption: A transport interruption never becomes completion merely because some text is already visible.

useCase.title: Streaming a troubleshooting explanation
useCase.situation: A broadband support assistant explains diagnostic steps while retrieving line-test results.
useCase.problem: Users perceive long silence as failure and resubmit the same question.
useCase.requirement: Show progress promptly while avoiding premature claims about the final diagnosis.
useCase.architecture: The gateway streams safe explanatory text but buffers structured diagnostic results until validated.
runtime: The client shows a generating state and receives the explanation incrementally.
A validated line-test result updates the answer, followed by an explicit completion event.
useCase.failure: If the connection drops, the client labels the visible answer interrupted and does not infer that troubleshooting completed.
useCase.impact: Measure first useful content, completion time, abandoned compute, and interrupted-stream rate; first-token speed alone can reward empty filler.

tradeoffs.cost: Limits the ability to retract unsafe or incorrect content.
Delays visible content and adds memory use.
Require connection capacity and slow-client handling.

failures.detection: Clients receive all chunks only at the end.
failures.recovery: Test the deployed transport path and configure buffering appropriately.

failures.detection: An incomplete argument stream triggers a tool call.
failures.recovery: Wait for complete validated tool-call data before dispatch.

mistakes.fix: Require an explicit terminal completion state.
Propagate cancellation to the provider and child tasks.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming a later filter can undo disclosure
mistakes.fix: Choose a release policy before emitting content.

whenToUse: Use when users benefit from meaningful incremental progress.
Use with clients that represent provisional and terminal states.
whenNotToUse: Avoid immediate release for output requiring whole-message approval.
Do not stream partial structured data into executing consumers.
Avoid streaming if infrastructure cannot support bounded connections.
checklist: Test proxy buffering and slow clients.
Measure first useful content and total completion time.
